fact: Remita's consumer app, launched 22 September 2026 in Lagos, supports instant transfers from Nigerian bank accounts to other African countries through PAPSS, per Remita's managing director.
Remita's app launched 22 September 2026 lets users transfer to anyone in Africa over PAPSS, per its managing director.

PAPSS chief executive Mike Ogbalu says Nigeria was among the first countries behind PAPSS and the first to chair its Permanent Council, and describes Nigerian transactions through the system in service.
Ogbalu says PAPSS carries significant transactions between Nigeria and Ghana, Rwanda and Kenya, with Nigerian traders paying electronically instead of carrying cash.
PAPSS CEO Mike Ogbalu said Nigeria was the first chair of the PAPSS Governing Council and continues to be a leader in its rollout.
The Bank of Ghana has started testing interoperability of CBDCs, stablecoins, bank accounts and mobile wallets with Rwanda and Nigeria, per Governor Asiama.
Governor Asiama said PAPSS has already been extended to mobile wallets along the Ghana-Nigeria corridor.
Governor Asiama described PAPSS as existing infrastructure in use on the Ghana-Nigeria corridor.

MoMo PSB, MTN Nigeria's payment service bank, sends wallet transfers from Nigeria to 16 African countries including Kenya and South Sudan and receives inbound transfers from the UK, US, Canada and Europe via Lightway Finance and Thunes.

Thunes says in a 25 November 2025 press release that MoMo PSB customers in Nigeria can now receive instant inbound remittances from the USA, UK, Canada, France, Australia, Saudi Arabia, Israel and South Africa through Thunes' Direct Global Network.
Nairametrics reports 22 Nigerian banks, the most of any country, are onboarded on PAPSS per its May 2025 participant list, and the CBN directed banks to originate PAPSS transactions.
